previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer was readmitted for severe nausea and bilious vomiting, just two days after a prior discharge. She was unable to tolerate oral intake or medications. Initial management included IV fluids and antiemetics, but hyponatremia developed, reaching a nadir of 128, attributed to SIADH from prolonged vomiting; this resolved with fluid restriction. Blood and urine cultures were negative, and leukocytosis was deemed stress-related. A chest X-ray showed no pulmonary cause for hyponatremia. An upper endoscopy revealed acute esophagitis, with no gastric abnormalities. Her gastric pacer was readjusted, leading to symptom improvement and tolerance of solid foods. Hypertension persisted during admission, prompting an increase in lisinopril to 10 mg daily and discontinuation of the clonidine patch due to its nausea-inducing side effects. She was discharged home in stable condition on optimized antiemetic and acid-suppression therapy, with follow-up scheduled for pacer evaluation and primary care management of blood pressure.

___ yo woman with DM Type I and gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer  
___, presents with severe nausea and vomiting for 1 day. She 
has been admitted ~ 10 times in the last 3 mths for the same 
symptoms, and was most recently discharge from ___ on ___. 
Patient states that she saw her GI doctor after been discharge 
approximately 7 days ago. He adjusted her gastric pacer and 
prescribed Protonix BID and Reglan QID. She had no episodes on 
nausea or vomitting for a total of 7 days until this morning. 
Today, she states that she got up feeling nauseaus and started 
to vomit light brown/greenish fluid several times. She attempted 
to take her morning pills, but vomitted right after. Her only 
intake for today was ice chips and gingerale which she vomitted 
immediatly after. She then came to the ER. She denies having any 
hematochezia, any abdominal pain, no changes in her bowel 
movement, no melena, no diarrhea, last BM this AM.  
During her previous hospitalization earlier this month, she was 
admitted for billious vomitting. She had an upper endoscopy  
to determine if there was an additional source of her symptoms  
other than gastroparesis. No such source was found. Endoscopy  
showed esophagitis, and biopsy confirmed this. Her gastric pacer 
was readjusted and she was able to tolerate solids and liquids 
by the time of her discharge.  
Prior to three months ago, she denies symptoms of  
gastroparesis after pacer placement: no nausea, no vomitting, no 
abdominal pain, no changes in her BM.  
.  
Her vitals in the ER were T 97.6 F , BP 193/108 HR 120s RR 16 
Pox 96 % on RA, FSG 140. In the ED, she was given IVF and Zofran 
8 mg, Reglan 10 mg IVx 2, compazine 10mg IV and metoprolol 5 mg 
IV.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo woman with DM Type I and gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer  
___, with multiple admissions in the last 3 months for severe 
nausea and vomiting who presents with same symptoms.  
.    
1. Gastroparesis: The patient's severe nausea and vomiting which 
is thought to be related to her gastroparesis. She has had  
multiple admissions over the past 3 months, seems to improve 
after adjustment of gastric pacer. During this hospitalization, 
patient was extremely nauseous and vomiting everything that she 
would drink or eat. She was placed in several antiemetics and 
prokinetic meds which included: Reglan, Zofran, Compazine, 
Ativan, and erythromycin. This showed to have   minimal effect 
on her nausea and had some improvement on her vomiting. We 
closely monitor electrolytes and she was given IV hydration. She 
had EGD done on ___ with Botox injection applied for 
sphincter relaxation in the pylorus. She was also noted to have 
ulcer of the mucosa with no bleeding on the gastroesophageal 
junction and lower third of the esophagus. These findings are 
compatible with reflux. GI recommended that she continues to 
take PPI BID and to have follow-up appointment.  She tolerated 
the procedure well and was feeling much improved post procedure. 
She had her diet advanced slow from clears to regular soft diet 
which she tolerated well. She was restarted on her home PO meds 
and discharged home. 
.  
.  
2. Hypertension/tachycardic: Patient was hypertensive in the ER 
193/108, possibly due to the nausea and active vomiting as well 
as not taking PO anti-hypertensive. She was given metoprolol 5 
mg Iv IV q6H and Hydralazine 20mg IV. Hypertension was 
moderately improved with hydralazine. Patient remained 
tachycardic with the HR on average on the 110s-120s. She was 
given IV fluids since it was initially thought this was related 
to dehydration, however it had minimal effect on HR. She was 
monitored on tele and continue to be on sinus tachy. On previous 
discharge summaries when patient was admitted for similar 
problem of nausea and vomiting she remained tachycardic for most 
of her previous admission. Both her HR and BP decreased with the 
resolution of her nausea and vomiting. This was thought to be 
related to sympathetic response. She was restart PO lisinopril 
once she was tolerating POs  
.

3. Diabetes Mellitus, type 1: FSG at admission was 140 -> 349.  
-Patient was initially given 20 units of Lantus since she was 
NPO, her FSG were elevated needing extra coverage during the 
night. Lantus dose was then increased to her normal home dose of 
28 units. FSG were better controlled. She was also placed on 
Humalog sliding scale. She is followed by ___ as outpatient.  

.  
FEN/GI: After EGD with Botox injection patient's nausea and 
vomiting improved. She was able to tolerate her a soft diabetic 
diet. During the hospitalization we monitor her electrolytes and 
on day prior to discharge her K was 2.9, we then replaced it.
